chapter: New York 1936-39 (second pass of the transcript)
title: Freddie Green, Snub Mosley and the Club Creole (second pass)
summary: Repeat of the club's other bands, famous visitors and the move to 54th Street.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, you know Hammond has written about going and hearing Freddie Green, that he was playing there with Teddy Clark and a bass player by the name of Frank Clark.
His brother, half-brother, yeah.
Well, when was that? That was after Skeets?
No, that was before.
That was before?
Yes. Snub Mosely was after that. You are aware of Snub Mosely?
Sure.
The man with the funny horn?
Funny horn, yeah.
He was after that, then us. And this is after my Savoy --
Yeah, right. And you said Mary Lou used to come and --
Mary Lou, everybody.
Everybody came.

Everybody. It was a must. John would have them as guests and then they would come and sit in. Dave Matthews, when he was with Harry James. Harry James himself. So, I met everybody. Betty, you know, I met everybody.
Yeah. And this went on for how long, I mean, you were with Talbot until the end of '38, or in '38, Teddy Wilson was in '39.
So how long did the Black Cat keep going though? You said Snub Mosely came in after --
Well, we moved up to another place on 54th Street, Club Creole where Amanda Randolph was --
With Skeets Talbot?
Yeah, and the place got closed down because of legalities, you know. So that was after -- and that club never made headlines, but it was, it was a real groovey place.
